case: memry-config.json exists and is not a JSON object, or cannot be read
typescript: The desktop store falls back to defaults (apps/desktop/src/main/store.ts:303-318): every command runs on an empty registry.
rust: Every command that reads the registry exits 1 with `the config file <path> could not be read: <reason>` and leaves the file as it is (AppConfig::load_strict). The app owns the file and sets a bad one aside at its next launch.
approval: #4278 (Step 35 follow-up 3, VERIFY-4885): safer than acting on an empty registry; recorded here.

case: the app or the vault still holds Electron data the import has not brought over, or the app is recovering the vault's data.db
typescript: The TypeScript CLI opened Electron's .memry/data.db and ran the command.
rust: Every command but `vault list|current|use|remove` exits 1 and creates nothing: `MemryNote has not finished updating your data. Open MemryNote once, then run this command again.` (import pending), `This vault still holds data of the previous MemryNote that was never brought over, so the command line cannot use it. Use this vault in MemryNote.` (core created over Electron's data.db), or `MemryNote is repairing this vault's database. Open MemryNote and let it finish, then run this command again.` (data.db.recovering present).
approval: #3552 Design, Opening a vault, as amended on #3552 (FIX-5055).

case: `vault reindex`: the counts it prints, and an index.db that needs a rebuild
typescript: Dropped and refilled the Electron search tables and printed the totals of that rebuild ({notes,tasks,inbox,skipped,durationMs}).
rust: Runs the app's own incremental pass (core Search::reindex) in one index.db transaction, so it never races the app's pass, and prints what this pass indexed: a second run right after the first prints 0 notes. An index.db that is damaged or newer than this build exits 1 with `The search index cannot be updated here (<reason>). Open MemryNote, which repairs it, then run this command again.` and stays byte for byte; only the app sets an index aside, because its open handles would lose the file.
approval: Pending Kaan's review on the Step 35 B2a PR (#3552); conservative default meanwhile.

case: `vault update-config` with a defaultNoteFolder or journalFolder that leads outside the vault (`../outside`, an absolute path)
typescript: ensureVaultFolders created that folder wherever it pointed, outside the vault included.
rust: Writes the key as given and prints the same config, but creates no folder outside the vault (a lexical check of the relative path).
approval: Pending Kaan's review on the Step 35 B2a PR (#3552); conservative default meanwhile.

case: the .memry/config.json that `vault config`, `vault update-config` and `vault set-icon` leave on disk
typescript: Every command, read commands included, rewrote a config.json that lacked a default key (defaultNoteFolder, journalFolder, journalDateFormat, attachmentsFolder) as `{...defaults, ...file}`, defaults first. Every write ended the file with a newline.
rust: A read command (`vault config`) leaves the file as it is and prints the same view. `vault update-config` and `vault set-icon` write through the app's own writer (memry_desktop::vault::config::update): the same keys and values as the TypeScript, in the file's own key order with any missing defaults after it, and no trailing newline. On a config the app wrote (excludePatterns first, every default present) the trailing newline is the only difference.
approval: Pending Kaan's review on the Step 35 B2a PR (#3552); conservative default meanwhile.
